purpose: Test whether Jev tier classification followed by Gemini ranking preserves final subject-assessment quality while improving complete-run latency or cost.
hypothesis: A two-stage Jev-tier and Gemini-rank assessment is non-inferior to the incumbent single Gemini 3.8 Flash assessment on the frozen tier and ranking evaluations, with lower complete-run provider cost or latency.

source.ground_truth: Existing immutable human-reviewed v11 labels only.

incumbent.operation: One production subject-assessment call that jointly assigns tiers, ranks each tier, and returns rationales and evidence citations.

candidate.tier_operation: One batched two-question request per subject using the unchanged full-day state and fixed 0.5 composition thresholds.
candidate.ranking_operation: One fixed-tier call per day that may order subjects and generate rationales and evidence citations but may not change tier membership.

tier_contract.context_policy: Refuse an over-guard candidate arm. Never clip, summarize, chunk, or silently substitute the incumbent.
tier_contract.failure_policy: Any missing or failed subject judgment makes the candidate arm unavailable and counts as the worst paired quality outcome.

ranking_contract.tier_membership: The response schema restricts each tier array to the Jev-composed subjects assigned to that tier.
ranking_contract.coverage: Every supplied subject appears exactly once and retains its fixed tier.
ranking_contract.ordering: Array position is a contiguous one-based semantic rank within the fixed tier.
ranking_contract.evidence: Every rationale is non-empty and every cited article belongs to the assessed subject and immutable input evidence.
ranking_contract.correction: At most one complete-response correction is allowed; both attempts remain in accounting.

execution.provider_reuse: Historical Jev results may be reported as context but are forbidden in measured latency and cost trials. Resume may reuse only exact terminal results from this experiment identity.
execution.checkpoint: Persist an in-flight marker before each provider dispatch and atomically record each attempt and terminal arm outcome.
execution.cost_policy: Include every accepted, rejected, corrected, retried, and failed provider attempt. Missing usage makes cost a lower bound, never zero.
execution.latency_policy: Measure wall time from arm entry through validated assessment output. Report summed provider-attempt latency separately for diagnosis.

required_metrics: completed, unavailable, and failed arm counts
tier exact accuracy and per-tier recall
complete subject coverage and contiguous tier ranks
promotion_gate: Zero invalid or incomplete candidate assessments.
Zero control-case regressions against the incumbent.
Candidate passes at least as many frozen tier and ranking cases as the incumbent.
No provider attempt or accounting gap is omitted from the report.
Complete-run latency and cost are reported without excluding failed or unavailable arms.
quality.interpretation: Passing permits a separate guarded rollout proposal. It does not change production by itself.
